title_en: The Creed of al-Ash'ari and His Retraction of It
body_ar: بعض الناس يقول إن عقيدة الأشعري غير صحيحة و أنه تراجع عنها قبل موته فما صحة ذلك؟ إ ن الإمام أبا الحسن علي بن إسماعيل الأشعري إمام من أئمة أهل السنة من المسلمين و هو من ذرية أبي موسى صاحب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم و قد اشتهر بحفظ الكتاب و السنة و إتقان علوم الدين و كان قد رأى أن الاجتهاد الذي وضعت فيه المذاهب اقتصر على الجانب الفقهي و لم يصل إلى الجانب العقدي فأراد أن يضع قواعد للمسلمين في العقيدة تكون مذهبا و قد كان في البداية على مذهب المعتزلة فرجع عنه و تاب منه. و رد عليهم بكثير من الردود و كتبه في ذلك موجودة منتشرة ثم لما وضع تلك القواعد كان منها بعض الإجتهادات الخاطئة التي هو مثاب عليها قطعا لأنه عرف منه الصلاح و الورع فما أصاب فيه فله فيه أجران و ما أخطأ فيه فله به أجر و تلك الأخطاء التي وقع فيها قد صرح هو برجوعه عنها في كتابه (مقالات الإسلاميين) و في كتابه (الإبانة عن أصول الديانة) و كلاهما مروي بالأسانيد المتصلة إلى المؤلف و قد ألف كذلك الحافظ بن عساكر كتابا سماه الذب عن الأشعري و هو كتاب مطبوع موجود فلهذا يعلم أن أبا الحسن قد رجع عن تلك الأخطاء التي وقع فيها و من رجع عن الخطإ فإنه لا يعد محسوبا عليه و بالأخص أن المذهب الذي ينسبه الناس إلى الأشعري كثير من مسائله لم يسمع بها الأشعري و لا قالها ولا وجدت في زمانه و لا في شيء من كتبه و إنما قالها المتأخرون من المتكلمين و إذا راجعتم كتب العقائد المؤلفة على ما يسمى بالمذهب الأشعري ستجدون أنهم يقولون خلافا للشيخ أبي الحسن و بعض الأقوال تنسب إليه فينكرها بعض الأشاعرة أنفسهم و لذلك قال السيوطي رحمه الله في الكوكب الساطع: يمتنع التقليد في العقائد و العنبري جوزه و قد حظر ثم على الأول إن يقلد لكن أبو هاشم لم يعتبر قال القشيري عليه مفترى الفخر و الأستاذ ثم الآمدي أسلافنا كالشافعي به النظر فمؤمن عاص على المعتمد إيمانه وقد عزي للأشعري فكثير من الأقوال التي تنسب إلى الأشعري لم يقل بها و أسانيدها غير صحيحة و لا توجد في شيء من كتبه أصلا و كثير منها يصرح أصحابه بأنهم خالفوا الشيخ أبا الحسن في ذلك كإثبات المعنويات الصفات السبع التي اشتهرت بالمعنويات أول من أثبتها الفخر الرازي و قد قال فيها إنه يخالف الشيخ أبا الحسن في ذلك صرح هو أنه يخالف الشيخ أبا الحسن في ذلك و لهذا قال الشيخ محمد المام رحمه الله: الاشْعَرِي الاحْوَالْ انْكَرْهَ وَ اْلفَخَرْ الرَّازِي حَرَّرْهَ عَنْهَ صِفَاتْ الرَّحْمَنْ فصاحب الفكرة هو الفخر الرازي و ليس الإمام أبا الحسن الأشعري فالأشعري إذن أنكر ذلك و على هذا فما ينسب إليه على أنه مذهب له مثل ما ينسب إلى الإمام مالك أنه مذهب له و كثير من الأقوال لم يقلها و لا هي في موطئه و لا في الكتب المروية عنه و لهذا قال الدبوسي من الحنفية قال: إن الأقوال المنسوبة إلى الأئمة و الفقه المدون في الكتب ينبغي أن يراجع فما كان منه من اجتهاد المجتهدين أخذ به و ما كان من اجتهاد المقلدين رد عليهم فكيف يجتهدون و هم لا يدعون الاجتهاد. هذا كلام الدبوسي من أئمة الحنفية مع أنه مقلد.
body_en:
Some people say that the creed of al-Ash'ari is not sound and that he retracted it before his death. What truth is there in that?

Imam Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Isma'il al-Ash'ari is one of the imams of Ahl al-Sunnah among the Muslims. He is a descendant of Abu Musa, the Companion of the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace. He was renowned for his memorisation of the Book and the Sunnah and for his mastery of the religious sciences. He had taken the view that the independent legal reasoning (ijtihād) in which the schools of law were laid down had been confined to the juristic side and had not reached the creedal side, so he wished to lay down principles for the Muslims in creed (ʿaqīdah) that would constitute a school. At the outset he had followed the school of the Mu'tazilah, then he retracted it and repented of it, and he refuted them with many refutations; his books on that are extant and in circulation.

Then, when he laid down those principles, among them were some erroneous exercises of independent reasoning for which he is certainly rewarded, because he was known for his uprightness and his scrupulousness: what he got right in it earns him two rewards, and what he got wrong in it earns him one reward. As for those errors into which he fell, he himself stated plainly that he retracted them, in his book Maqalat al-Islamiyyin and in his book al-Ibanah 'an Usul al-Diyanah — both of which are transmitted with chains of transmission (asānīd) connected back to the author. Likewise the ḥāfiẓ Ibn Asakir composed a book which he named al-Dhabb 'an al-Ash'ari, and it is a printed, available book. For this reason it is known that Abu al-Hasan did retract those errors into which he had fallen; and whoever retracts an error, it is not reckoned against him.

This is so all the more because, of the school that people ascribe to al-Ash'ari, there are many questions that al-Ash'ari never heard of, never said, and which did not exist in his time nor in any of his books; rather it was the later theologians (mutakallimūn) who said them. If you consult the books of creed composed according to what is called the Ash'ari school, you will find that they say things contrary to Shaykh Abu al-Hasan; and there are positions ascribed to him which some of the Ash'aris themselves reject. That is why al-Suyuti — may God have mercy on him — said in al-Kawkab al-Sati':

*Following a qualified scholar (taqlīd) is impermissible in matters of creed — and al-'Anbari permitted it, and it has been prohibited — then, upon the first position, if one does follow — but Abu Hashim did not reckon it — al-Qushayri said: it is a fabrication against him — al-Fakhr, and al-Ustadh, then al-Amidi — our predecessors, such as al-Shafi'i: with him lies the considered view — then he is a believer who is disobedient, upon the relied-upon position — his faith; and that has been ascribed to al-Ash'ari.*

Many of the positions ascribed to al-Ash'ari are ones he did not hold; their chains of transmission are not sound, and they are not found in any of his books at all. With many of them his own followers state plainly that they departed from Shaykh Abu al-Hasan in the matter — such as the affirmation of the maʿnawiyyāt, the seven attributes that became known as the maʿnawiyyāt. The first to affirm them was al-Fakhr al-Razi, and he said concerning them that he was departing from Shaykh Abu al-Hasan in that; he himself stated plainly that he departs from Shaykh Abu al-Hasan in that. That is why Shaykh Muhammad al-Mamm — may God have mercy on him — said:

*Al-Ash'ari denied the states (aḥwāl), and it was al-Fakhr al-Razi who worked out from them the attributes of the All-Merciful.*

So the author of the idea is al-Fakhr al-Razi, and not Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari. Al-Ash'ari, then, denied that. On this basis, what is ascribed to him as being a school of his is like what is ascribed to Imam Malik as being a school of his: many of the positions he did not state, nor are they in his Muwatta', nor in the books transmitted from him. That is why al-Dabusi of the Hanafis said — he said: the positions ascribed to the imams, and the jurisprudence set down in the books, ought to be reviewed. Whatever of it comes from the independent reasoning of those qualified to exercise it is to be taken; and whatever comes from the reasoning of those who merely follow a qualified scholar is to be rejected — for how can they exercise independent reasoning when they do not even claim to be capable of it? This is the statement of al-Dabusi, one of the imams of the Hanafis, even though he was himself a follower of a school.

flags.arabic: يمتنع التقليد في العقائد و العنبري جوزه و قد حظر ثم على الأول إن يقلد لكن أبو هاشم لم يعتبر قال القشيري عليه مفترى الفخر و الأستاذ ثم الآمدي أسلافنا كالشافعي به النظر فمؤمن عاص على المعتمد إيمانه وقد عزي للأشعري
flags.context: the quotation from al-Suyuti's al-Kawkab al-Sati' on taqlid in creed
options: translate the hemistichs in the order the source gives them, marked as scrambled, and leave reconstruction to the reviewer
reconstruct the couplets from the rhyme and translate the reconstructed text
omit the quotation until the correct text is supplied
flags.note: CRITICAL. These lines were published in a two-column verse table and the CMS text extraction has flattened them column-first, so the hemistichs no longer stand in their true order and the couplets are broken apart. The rhyme words fall into three clean groups of three — العقائد/يقلد/المعتمد, حظر/يعتبر/النظر, مفترى/الآمدي/الأشعري — which confirms the scrambling but does not by itself fix the order. Two pairings are strongly indicated on rhyme and sense ('ثم على الأول إن يقلد' with 'فمؤمن عاص على المعتمد'; 'لكن أبو هاشم لم يعتبر' with 'إيمانه وقد عزي للأشعري'), but I have not reconstructed the passage, because guessing here would put words into al-Suyuti's mouth and, through him, into the Sheikh's argument. The English follows the source order and reads as disjointed prose; that is deliberate. The Sheikh's office should supply the passage from a printed al-Kawkab al-Sati'. 66 tatweel (U+0640) padding characters from the same table were removed from body_ar — declared normalisation, not a silent fix.

flags.context: the whole record: the Sheikh defends al-Ash'ari and attributes the disputed doctrines to later theologians
options: publish with the Sheikh's position stated as he gives it
flags.note: Editorially sensitive under style guide section 12. The status of al-Ash'ari and the Ash'ari school is a live and heated dispute; the Sheikh here defends him, treats the criticised positions as later accretions, and grades him a rewarded mujtahid even in error. Read in English out of context this will be quoted on both sides. Translated exactly as given, neither softened nor strengthened. The decision whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.context: the attribution of a book to Ibn Asakir
options: render the title exactly as the Sheikh gives it and flag
render it with the full known title
flags.note: Ibn Asakir's defence of al-Ash'ari is generally known under a longer title; 'al-Dhabb ʿan al-Ashʿari' is how the Sheikh names it here. Rendered exactly as given — style guide section 6 forbids silently correcting an apparent error in the source — and flagged so a reviewer can decide whether the Sheikh is using a short form or the transcription has shortened it.

flags.arabic: كإثبات المعنويات الصفات السبع التي اشتهرت بالمعنويات
flags.context: the example of a doctrine ascribed to al-Ash'ari by his own followers
options: the maʿnawiyyāt, the seven attributes that became known as the maʿnawiyyāt
flags.note: A technical kalām term with no glossary entry. Left transliterated with the Sheikh's own gloss beside it rather than given an English rendering that would prejudge the doctrine. Note that this passage is kalām, so the section 8 exemption applies throughout: nothing here is one of the five legal rulings.

flags.arabic: الاشْعَرِي الاحْوَالْ انْكَرْهَ وَ اْلفَخَرْ الرَّازِي حَرَّرْهَ عَنْهَ صِفَاتْ الرَّحْمَنْ
flags.context: a line quoted from Shaykh Muhammad al-Mamm
options: al-Ash'ari denied the states (aḥwāl), and it was al-Fakhr al-Razi who worked out from them the attributes of the All-Merciful
al-Ash'ari denied the states, and al-Fakhr al-Razi separated the attributes of the All-Merciful from them
al-Ash'ari denied the states, and al-Fakhr al-Razi established the attributes of the All-Merciful in place of them
flags.note: This line is in Hassaniyya, the Mauritanian dialect, not in classical Arabic, and it is vocalised in the source in dialect orthography ('انْكَرْهَ', 'حَرَّرْهَ', 'عَنْهَ'). 'حرّره عنه' is the uncertain element: it can carry 'derived from', 'distinguished from' or 'settled in place of'. The surrounding prose supports the first reading, since the Sheikh's point is that al-Razi, not al-Ash'ari, originated the doctrine. A Mauritanian reader should confirm before this is fixed.

translator_notes: This is one of the few records in this range with a real written answer, and the Sheikh gives his own position unambiguously, so it is typed 'fatwa' and is not affected by style guide section 10.
The reward formula 'two rewards if right, one if wrong' is the Sheikh's own phrasing; he does not cite it as a hadith, so no attribution or grading has been added to the English.

'المقلدين' is rendered by the glossary's non-pejorative sense, 'those who merely follow a qualified scholar', and the closing 'مقلد' said of al-Dabusi likewise — the Arabic is descriptive, not abusive, and the point turns on that.

Positions reported from others — al-'Anbari, Abu Hashim, al-Qushayri, al-Fakhr al-Razi, al-Amidi, al-Dabusi — are kept visibly attributed throughout and are nowhere collapsed into the Sheikh's own view.
The source writes 'إ ن' with a space at the start of the answer and 'الخطإ' with the hamza on a kasra seat; both are left as served.
